title: MVP (Minimum Viable Product)
seoTitle: What Is an MVP? Minimum Viable Product Explained
seoDescription: An MVP is the smallest version of a product that real users can use to prove an idea. What to include, what to leave out, typical timelines and costs in India.
summary: An MVP (Minimum Viable Product) is the smallest version of a product that lets real users complete one important job, so you can learn whether the idea works before investing in everything else. It is minimal in scope, not in quality: security, data and analytics still need to be done properly.

dataPoints.label: Typical timeline
dataPoints.value: 8–12 weeks for a focused first version

dataPoints.label: Must include
dataPoints.value: One core user journey end to end, log-in and security, analytics, a way to collect feedback

dataPoints.label: Leave out
dataPoints.value: Secondary user types, advanced settings, automation a person can do manually at first

dataPoints.label: Success measure
dataPoints.value: Agreed before launch: activation, retention and one business outcome

body:
## What makes a good MVP

A good MVP tests one clear question, such as "will distributors reorder through an app instead of calling?" Everything in it serves that test.

## Common mistakes

- Building for every user type at once.
- Treating the MVP as throwaway and cutting security or data design.
- Launching without a plan to reach real users.

Read [how to scope an MVP that ships in ten weeks](/blog/mvp-development-how-to-scope-a-first-version-that-ships-in-ten-weeks).

faqs.q: Is an MVP the same as a prototype?
faqs.a: No. A prototype shows how something might work, often without real data. An MVP is working software real users rely on.

faqs.q: Should the MVP be an app or a website?
faqs.a: Whichever your core users already use for similar tasks. A web app is often faster to launch and change.
